homework: Spend 10 minutes reflecting on how Tawheed shapes a decision you face this week and jot a concrete change.
Match three divine attributes from the lesson to people you admire and say a dua thanking Allah for each.
Share a short explanation of Tawheed with a study partner and invite their questions.
Memorize a short dua about Allah's oneness and recite it before sleep while focusing on its meaning.
Read a verse slowly with translation, record one insight, and ask Allah to help you live it for the next day.
Listen to a two-minute recitation, note the cadence, and repeat the verse aloud three times in your own voice.
Talk through a verse’s lesson with a mentor and write a short reflection about how it relates to your routine.
Plan a weekly rhythm (e.g., 3 sessions of 10 minutes) for Qur'anic reflection and mark it in your calendar.
Read one Prophetic story highlighting mercy, jot how you can mirror that trait in a current relationship.
Choose a Sunnah habit (greeting, charity, patience) to practice deliberately and record your progress daily.
Explain a seerah moment to a friend and ask them how it helps them see the Prophet anew.
Pray a short dua asking for patience and mercy while remembering the Prophet’s attitude during hardship.
List each of the five pillars with a practical goal (e.g., patience, service) so the rituals feel meaningful.
Design a micro version of one pillar you can do this week even if time is tight and track it daily.
Teach a pillar insight to someone curious and ask how it would fit into their routine.
Identify one resource (book, mentor, video) that clarifies a pillar you still find unfamiliar.
Track your five daily prayers for a full week, noting how presence changed each time.
Set up a calm prayer corner, remove one distraction, and test the new space for three prayers.
After one prayer, spend two minutes thanking Allah for three blessings you noticed that day.
Share a short dua you whispered in salah with a companion and invite them to pray for you.
Plan a fasting mindset by choosing one empathy-building prompt (e.g., think of someone hungry) for each day of next week.
Schedule a simple charity action (meal, gift, dua) to accompany iftar or suhoor and follow through.
Pick one night to recite extra Qur’an or dua with intention and note how it refreshed your focus.
List one Ramadan habit you want to keep after the month ends and create a reminder to keep it going.
Perform a deliberate act of kindness for someone you disagree with and record how it felt.
Identify one trigger that shortens your patience, pause before responding, and turn to dhikr.
Praise someone quietly for a humane action to reinforce generosity and adab.
Say a dua asking Allah to soften your heart and keep a log of how you felt afterward.
Practice active listening in one conversation: summarize before replying and note what changed.
Identify a boundary you need to uphold and communicate it with respectful language.
Perform a small act that affirms someone’s worth (message, help, dua) especially if they feel unseen.
Include a dua for peace in your daily routine (e.g., after salah or before bed).
Compare two prophets from the chapter: list how their trials echo your own journey and write one lesson from each.
Share one prophetic story with someone and ask how it inspires their hope.
Practice patience when facing rejection by recalling a prophet who kept trusting Allah.
Schedule ten minutes to learn a new fact about a lesser-known prophet to broaden your perspective.
Plan a respectful visit to a mosque (or virtual tour), noting what made it welcoming or still mysterious.
Volunteer for a small task (cleaning, greeting, charity) that supports the mosque community.
Reflect on a khutbah or talk you hear and write down one practical takeaway.
Invite a friend to join a mosque event and explain why the space matters to you.
Audit one area of your lifestyle (food, speech, media) leaving a note about how to align it with halal integrity.
Practice honest communication in a tricky situation, focusing on respect and transparency.
Support a halal business by expressing thanks to its owner and noticing the difference integrity makes.
Make a dua asking Allah to simplify halal choices when decisions feel confusing.
Reflect on how mutual respect looks in a relationship you value and plan one appreciative gesture.
Model healthy boundaries by clearly asking for space or time when needed with calm tone.
Challenge one stereotype gently when it arises by sharing facts or personal reflections.
Pray for equity between men and women and note how the words shape your interactions.
Write a short after-shahada plan: prayer, Quran, community, mentoring, and follow it for a week.
Reach out to a mentor or welcome team and describe one question you need support with.
Teach a new Muslim or curious friend a simple dua and explain its meaning.
Celebrate a milestone (first prayer, learning a surah, meeting someone) with gratitude notes.
Plan one inclusive act for Eid (charity, meal, call) that keeps gratitude center stage.
Write down the Prophet’s sacrifice story and link it to a joyful obedience you can practice.
Invite someone who might feel isolated to celebrate with you, offering sincere welcome.
Schedule a moment to reflect on mercy during Eid by reciting takbeer and offering dua for others.
Review your daily actions and list deeds you hope will weigh on the right side of the scale.
Ask Allah for forgiveness, then forgive someone else to practice holding hope and accountability together.
Do one kind act today as an investment for the hereafter and note how it felt.
Make a nightly reminder (note, alarm, dua) that the akhira motivates your choices.
